runs.name: Run 7: live shadow test of the retrained own-data scorer
runs.text: 2026-11-11, AWS Academy Learner Lab, one t3.large node, SECOND_OPINION_MODE=shadow, scorer = second-opinion/models/own.joblib (47 trials, 115 windows: runs 3, 4 and 5-early). Started 18:40 UTC, stopped at its 80 minute deadline after 7 of 11 planned trials (84 minutes): a stuck APILatencyHigh alert kept each trial waiting 10-25 minutes for quiet.

runs.name: Run 8: live shadow test with the fault-start fix
runs.text: 2026-11-12, same AWS Academy Learner Lab instance as run 7, SECOND_OPINION_MODE=shadow, scorer = second-opinion/models/own.joblib (unchanged), engine and scorer rebuilt from the branch with the fix (estimate_fault_start: the start comes from the deciding alert minus its own for: delay, sent as fault_start). The pod printed new code: True before the harness started. All pods in autosre and monitoring were restarted fi

runs.name: Run 9: the stale-alert test (6 of 6 trials)
runs.text: 2026-11-12, same instance as runs 7 and 8, --stale mode of live_validate.py, engine and scorer with the fault-start fix. Each trial first turns on gateway latency so APILatencyHigh fires (about 91 s later) and lets it age 120 s, then injects the real fault on top. runs.name: Run 10: void (a deployment mistake, no data)
runs.text: 2026-11-12, planned as the third post-fix session: 3 trials per cause plus 5 unknown-cause, with the retrained model. It ran 11 trials from 03:52 to 06:29 UTC and recorded nothing: every trial says "no incident received before the timeout", 0 records each.

runs.name: Run 11
runs.text: Third post-fix session. Commit c6cb6ef, scorer model b565d77f (retrained on runs 3, 4, 5-early and 8), SECOND_OPINION_MODE=shadow. Harness started 07:54 UTC, finished 10:29 UTC (155 minutes), 14 trials (3 per known cause, 5 with no known cause). Results are in s3://autosre-validation-841736140404/results-run11/.

runs.name: Run 12
runs.text: Fourth post-fix session, run to close the volume gap left by run 11. Commit 72d91ec, scorer model b565d77f, SECOND_OPINION_MODE=shadow. Started 10:42 UTC, stopped at its 100-minute deadline at 12:24 UTC after 9 trials (planned 12: 4 per known cause, no unknown-cause trials because that criterion was already met). Results are in s3://autosre-validation-841736140404/results-run12/.

runs.name: Run 13
runs.text: Fifth post-fix session and the first run on the retrained scorer b565d77f alone, to build evidence for that model without pooling in older versions. Commit e9d588f, SECOND_OPINION_MODE=shadow. Harness started 13:43 UTC and stopped at its 190-minute deadline at 16:55 UTC after 16 trials (6 per cause planned; no unknown-cause trials). Results are in s3://autosre-validation-841736140404/results-run13/.

runs.name: Run 14
runs.text: Sixth post-fix session, run on a freshly started lab to top up the retrained scorer b565d77f after run 13 fell short. Commit bd3c797 (the harness with the contamination retry), SECOND_OPINION_MODE=shadow. Harness started 17:52 UTC and stopped at its 120-minute deadline at 19:53 UTC after 7 trials (3 per cause planned, no unknown-cause trials because that criterion was already met). Results are in s3://autosre-validat

runs.name: Run 15: Run 15 and the stuck-APILatencyHigh investigation
runs.text: Why trials were lost to "contamination" (an APILatencyHigh that would not clear), what was measured on the live cluster, and a short confirmation run. Session 2026-11-12, fresh lab, same instance, scorer b565d77f, SECOND_OPINION_MODE=shadow. Results of the confirmation run: s3://autosre-validation-841736140404/results-run15/.

runs.name: Run 16: the ambiguity rule and the gate, measured on and off
runs.text: Two open decisions, ESCALATE_ON_AMBIGUITY and SECOND_OPINION_MODE=gate, had only been judged from the simulator and from shadow-mode logs. These sessions ran them live, with two real faults injected together. Session 2026-11-12/13, fresh lab, scorer b565d77f, service CPU limit 1000m (see docs/live-validation-run15/summary.md), commit 1fd4eea. Raw results: s3://autosre-validation-841736140404/results-run16/ and result

runs.name: Real AWS validation
runs.text: The RCA pipeline tested against real failures of the lab's own resources, with no chaos endpoint and no event sent to the engine. Sessions 2026-11-13, lab instance i-04f8f4d75378a1aba, scorer b565d77f, as deployed: gate in shadow, ESCALATE_ON_AMBIGUITY off, services at the manifests' 200m CPU limits. Raw results: s3://autosre-validation-841736140404/results-real1/ to results-real7/. Driver: real_aws_validate.py; numb

runs.text: First run with the real memory slowness: trial 1 passed. Then it showed a runner bug (below): after the memory trial the scale-down kept the pod that still held the leak, the alert fired again and the dispatcher, correctly, scaled out a second time, which contaminated the next trial. Relaunched as comp13; the launcher's restore ran and safe defaults were confirmed
